summary: This document (swarm card L5) is a structured research-discussion proposal in the longevity/NAD biology space. It frames a specific, pre-registered experimental question: whether a residual CD38-inhibitor pulse outperforms a matched NAD-precursor pulse (NMN/NR) in raising tissue NAD after senolytic clearance of senescent/SASP cells. The claim is currently UNKNOWN (no head-to-head data exists), and the document explicitly classifies itself as a research discussion with a proposed assay design, not a completed experiment.

content_blocks.title: Document Metadata & Classification
content_blocks.content: Swarm ID: L5. Status: NEGATIVE (polarity: negative). Lane: longevity. Risk class: research-discussion. Novelty: subtract-before-add. Method: propose-assay. OpenLabs target: discussion (PASS_NEGATIVE — not claim). IP class: subtract-before-add; vault_hold=no; kill_cost_tier=2; time_to_refute=6 weeks. Related prior: L3 (precursor diminishing returns — separate UNKNOWN; not residual-ranking proof). Document is a PUBLIC_REPORT_ONLY.

content_blocks.title: Core Claim
content_blocks.content: After documented senescent-cell / SASP clearance lowers CD38 load, a residual CD38-inhibitor pulse raises tissue NAD more than a matched NAD-precursor pulse at the same post-clearance timepoint. Pre-registered threshold: ΔNAD_CD38i − ΔNAD_precursor ≥ 20% of the larger arm (or CD38i wins on a pre-registered superiority test). This is a PREDICTION, not an observed result — the head-to-head residual ranking is explicitly UNKNOWN.

content_blocks.title: Mechanism Sketch
content_blocks.content: Subtract-before-add framework: (1) Clear SASP-driven CD38+ macrophage load first (senolysis). (2) Pulse leftover levers (CD38i vs NAD precursor). Mechanistic rationale: CD38 gates age-related NAD decline and NMN degradation; senescent/SASP ablation lowers CD38 and partially restores NAD; ecto-CD38 block raises NAD via an NMN-dependent route; 78c-class CD38i improves aged-mouse healthspan as monotherapy. Competing caveat: after CD38↓, the residual CD38i target may shrink; because ecto-block is NMN-dependent, residual precursor may win once CD38 is already low — opposite ranking to the seed prediction.

content_blocks.title: Baseline Claims
content_blocks.content: Claimed baseline: After senolysis, residual CD38 inhibition and residual NAD precursor are interchangeable NAD boosters, or stacking both is always better than ranking which residual lever wins. Measured baseline (literature): CD38 gates age NAD/NMN fate (PMID 27304511); SASP→CD38+ macrophages→tissue NAD↓ (PMID 33199924); clearance ↓CD38 + partial NAD rebound; ecto-block NMN-dependent (PMID 33199925); 78c aged-mouse benefit as monotherapy (PMID 35263032). Post-clearance H2H residual ΔNAD CD38i vs precursor: UNKNOWN (PubMed soft-complete 0). Residual ranking margin ≥20%: PREDICTION.

content_blocks.title: Prior Art / Supporting Literature
content_blocks.content:
1. PMID 27304511 / DOI 10.1016/j.cmet.2016.05.006 / PMC4911708 — Camacho-Pereira 2016: Age NAD↓ requires CD38; CD38 is major in vivo NMN-degrading activity.
2. PMID 33199924 / DOI 10.1038/s42255-020-00305-3 / PMC7908681 — Covarrubias 2020: SASP induces CD38-high macrophages that reduce tissue NAD.
3. PMID 33199925 / DOI 10.1038/s42255-020-00298-z / PMC8752031 — Chini 2020: Senescent/SASP ablation ↓CD38 and partially restores NAD; ecto-CD38 block raises NAD NMN-dependently.
4. PMID 35263032 / DOI 10.1111/acel.13589 / PMC9009115 — Tarragó 2022: CD38i 78c improves median survival/healthspan in aged mice; monotherapy, not post-senolysis residual ranking.

content_blocks.title: Proposed Assay Design (Ablate / Refute / Ask a Human)
content_blocks.content:
Ablation logic: (1) Remove post-clearance residual 2-arm contrast (CD38i vs precursor at matched timepoint) → without H2H residual pulse, solo CD38i or precursor literature cannot rank which lever wins after subtract. (2) Remove documented clearance run-in with CD38↓/partial NAD rebound verification → without subtract-first confirmation, card collapses into generic CD38i-vs-precursor comparison. (3) Remove competing NMN-dependent/residual-target-shrink caveat as allowed falsifier → ignoring flip risk would overclaim seed ranking.

Refutation criterion: On the pre-registered post-clearance panel, residual precursor ΔNAD ≥ residual CD38i ΔNAD (or the ≥20% CD38i-superiority margin fails) when CD38↓ is verified — especially under low residual CD38 activity.

Human review asks: Lock tissue (WAT/liver), clearance verification (CD38 activity + SC/SASP marker), and identical post-clearance sampling before ranking arms; do not treat L3 as already deciding residual ranking; no dosing. Estimated time to refute: 6 weeks.

content_blocks.title: Actionable Limitations
content_blocks.content:
1. Do not treat L3 as proving L5 — L3 left precursor diminishing returns UNKNOWN; this card ranks residual CD38i vs residual precursor.
2. After clearance, residual CD38i ΔNAD may shrink because the target fell — CD38i>precursor is not implied by CD38↓ alone.
3. NMN-dependent ecto-block implies residual precursor may regain efficacy when CD38 is already low — competing PREDICTION.

key_findings: The core claim (CD38i pulse > NAD-precursor pulse post-senolysis) is explicitly classified as UNKNOWN — no head-to-head experimental data exists (PubMed soft-complete 0).

All supporting mechanistic evidence is from published literature (TRL 1–2 level): CD38 gates age NAD decline (PMID 27304511), SASP-driven CD38+ macrophages reduce tissue NAD (PMID 33199924), senolytic clearance lowers CD38 and partially restores NAD with NMN-dependent ecto-block (PMID 33199925), and 78c CD38i improves aged-mouse healthspan as monotherapy (PMID 35263032).
No original experimental data is presented in this document; it is a structured research-discussion / propose-assay card.
Pre-registered superiority threshold defined: ΔNAD_CD38i − ΔNAD_precursor ≥ 20% of the larger arm, or CD38i wins on a pre-registered superiority test.
A competing prediction is explicitly acknowledged: residual NAD precursor may outperform CD38i post-senolysis if CD38 activity is already low (NMN-dependent ecto-block logic from PMID 33199925).
Estimated time to refute the claim: 6 weeks (kill_cost_tier=2).
Proposed model systems: aged tissue (WAT/liver) or SASP-conditioned system with senolytic/SASP-ablation run-in → wash → 2-arm residual pulse design.
CD38i 78c showed ~10% median survival improvement in aged mice as monotherapy (PMID 35263032), but this is not a post-senolysis factorial — cannot be used to rank residual levers.
Document is TRL 1: concept/mechanism only, with a proposed assay but no completed experiments.
